verses.text: Thus the Lord Yahweh showed me: and behold, he formed locusts in the beginning of the shooting up of the latter growth; and behold, it was the latter growth after the king’s harvest.
When they finished eating the grass of the land, then I said, “Lord Yahweh, forgive, I beg you! How could Jacob stand? For he is small.”
Yahweh relented concerning this. “It shall not be,” says Yahweh.
Thus the Lord Yahweh showed me and behold, the Lord Yahweh called for judgment by fire; and it dried up the great deep, and would have devoured the land.
Then I said, “Lord Yahweh, stop, I beg you! How could Jacob stand? For he is small.”
Yahweh relented concerning this. “This also shall not be,” says the Lord Yahweh.
Thus he showed me and behold, the Lord stood beside a wall made by a plumb line, with a plumb line in his hand.
Yahweh said to me, “Amos, what do you see?” I said, “A plumb line.” Then the Lord said, “Behold, I will set a plumb line in the middle of my people Israel. I will not again pass by them any more.
The high places of Isaac will be desolate, the sanctuaries of Israel will be laid waste; and I will rise against the house of Jeroboam with the sword.”
Then Amaziah the priest of Bethel sent to Jeroboam king of Israel, saying, “Amos has conspired against you in the middle of the house of Israel. The land is not able to bear all his words.
For Amos says, ‘Jeroboam will die by the sword, and Israel shall surely be led away captive out of his land.’”
Amaziah also said to Amos, “You seer, go, flee away into the land of Judah, and there eat bread, and prophesy there:
but don’t prophesy again any more at Bethel; for it is the king’s sanctuary, and it is a royal house!”
Then Amos answered Amaziah, “I was no prophet, neither was I a prophet’s son; but I was a herdsman, and a farmer of sycamore figs;
and Yahweh took me from following the flock, and Yahweh said to me, ‘Go, prophesy to my people Israel.’
Now therefore listen to Yahweh’s word: ‘You say, Don’t prophesy against Israel, and don’t preach against the house of Isaac.’

Therefore Yahweh says: ‘Your wife shall be a prostitute in the city, and your sons and your daughters shall fall by the sword, and your land shall be divided by line; and you yourself shall die in a land that is unclean, and Israel shall surely be led away captive out of his land.’”

footnotes.content: The Lord let Amos see what was coming—a terrible hunger that would strip the land bare. But notice: the vision came BEFORE the judgment, not after. Grace always shows us what's at stake before it destroys.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Amos cried out the instant he understood the danger. He knew Israel deserved it, and yet his first word was 'forgive'—because he also knew Israel was small and broken. The prophet's heart broke before the Lord's judgment fell.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: One prayer. One intercession. And Yahweh turned back. I've learned that the Lord is never eager to judge—He waits to hear if anyone will plead for mercy. Someone's faithful cry changes everything.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Now fire. A judgment 'called for'—more terrible than locusts because this one came from the throne itself. It dried up the sources of life. When we turn from the Lord, even the deep will rise against us.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Again Amos cried out. This time he didn't wait to see the damage—his heart moved before the fire fell. When we love a people, we intercede before judgment completes its work.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Yahweh relented. Twice now the intercessor's plea has bent the knee of heaven. We forget how much power the Lord has given to a faithful voice. Amos bought his people a little more time to repent.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Now the third vision: the plumb line. In construction, a plumb line shows what's true and what's crooked. Israel had drifted so far from the mark that even the Lord's measuring line would reveal how far they had fallen—and how little grace could prop them up.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The Lord spoke Amos's own name—'Amos, what do you see?' He was calling the prophet to witness and speak truth. Then came the hard word: 'I will not again pass by them.' No more mercy after the measuring.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The high places—the altars where Israel had mixed their worship with foreign gods. Jeroboam's house, built on counterfeit faith. When we build on sand, the wind comes and the house falls. The sword of the Lord will not miss what His eye has measured.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Amaziah the priest heard Amos and saw a threat, not a warning. How quickly power reaches for silencing. The land 'cannot bear his words'—meaning, the king cannot bear to hear the truth. Pride always calls truth a conspiracy.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Amaziah twisted Amos's prophecy, making it sound like political sedition. This is how power works: it takes a shepherd's faithful word and rewrites it as treason. But Amos had not made up what he saw.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Amaziah offered Amos a deal: flee to Judah, be safe, keep your trade. Go somewhere else and prophesy where it's comfortable. Many voices in our age whisper the same: hide the truth, or tell it where no one in power will hear.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Bethel was the king's sanctuary, a royal house—meaning God had been domesticated, turned into a tool of the throne. Amaziah could not permit a word that might trouble the king's god. But the Lord is not the king's possession.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Amos's answer: I was no prophet by trade or inheritance. I was a herdsman tending figs. He spoke his truth plainly—I did not choose this office; the Lord chose me. A sheep farmer called to speak what he had seen. No credentials but the calling.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Yahweh took him from the flock and said 'Prophesy to my people.' No school, no apprenticeship—just a direct call and a command. The Lord makes His prophets. He doesn't need human approval or a priest's blessing.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Amos turned the priest's own prohibition back on him: You've commanded me not to prophesy against Israel and Isaac. But Amos had been faithful to speak exactly what the Lord showed. The priest's order could not erase the Lord's call.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Readers today hear an echo in Amos's final words to Amaziah—how often have we seen the silencer silenced, the one who tells the prophet 'go elsewhere' find themselves far from home, facing what they tried to prevent? The Lord settles accounts with those who oppose His word.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight
